messages:
Priya: Quick sketch - we need a lightweight read-contract for active/active that lets product choose PII-safe reads without forcing full synchronous cross-region replication for all traffic. ideas?
Carlos: +1. Can we separate "visibility" (what a read can return) from "durability" (where the canonical copy is)? For PII we require visibility to be resident-anchored.
Yvonne: Proposal: introduce Read-Consistency header with 3 levels: `local-fast`, `resident-anchored`, `strict-linearizable`. Default `local-fast`. Product opts per-route/tenant.
Dan: How does `resident-anchored` work under the hood? My thought: attach a residency-assertion token to writes when resident persistence completes. Readers query local cache; if record has token -> return. If missing -> reader proxies read to resident region (sync) or returns 202/pending depending on route policy.
Priya: We should avoid proxying reads for high-QPS non-PII paths. So allow a non-blocking fallback: return stale local copy + a `X-Redwood-Visibility` header explaining freshness and a `residency_status` token for clients that will revalidate.
Carlos: Token design: short-lived signed proof minted by resident region on final-persist. Fields: tenant_id, object_id, sequence, issued_at, sig. Reader can validate token locally (sig key cached) to know it's resident-anchored. That avoids round-trips for many reads.
Yvonne: Edge case: if resident region died and token can't be minted, `resident-anchored` reads should either 503 or return explicit pending. Need legal input on acceptable behavior.
legal-bot: (automated) For EU-residency contracts we require that any read that surfaces PII must only return data if resident-anchored proof exists OR if origin region is EU. Otherwise deny/503. Logs must record proof verification.
Dan: Implementation pieces: resident-proof issuer service + key rotation + local validator in data plane + read-proxy fallback + SDK flagging. Also new metric `resident_proof_issuance_latency`.
Priya: What about ordering? If reads rely on token sequence, clients that require monotonicity should also include `min_seq` in request and get 409 if not satisfied. Similar to conditional GET.
Carlos: Good. API sketch:
```
GET /v1/objects/:id
Headers:
  X-Read-Consistency: local-fast|resident-anchored|min-seq=1234
Responses:
  200 OK (body, X-Redwood-Visibility: resident-anchored|stale|pending, X-Resident-Token: <jwt>)
  202 Accepted (pending resident anchoring)
  403 Forbidden (residency violation)
  409 Conflict (min-seq not met)
```
Yvonne: Runbook/ops guidance:
- Alert if `resident_proof_issuance_latency` > threshold and resident-proof failure-rate spikes
- `proof_issuer:errors` SLO and small fanout retry window
- Expose admin endpoints: `GET /admin/proof/{tenant}/{object}` to inspect proofs and issue a manual proof for recovery
ops-bot: [automated] Note: deploy of resident-proof service will be part of next canary on 2026-04-10. Expect additional VARs.
Priya: Testing matrix: normal local reads, resident-anchored happy path, delayed proof issuance, resident down -> request behavior (503 vs stale) for different tenant policies, key-rotation window causing verifier rejects.
Dan: Security: resident token signing keys must be stored in KMS/HSM and verification keys rotated via signed keyset metadata. Add telemetry for key-reuse and failed-sig counts.
Carlos: SDK: provide `readConsistency` option and helpers to surface visibility header to app devs so they can show a "pending" banner in UI.
Yvonne: Migration: default tenants remain `local-fast`. Add tenant-level residency policy that maps to read defaults. Product can flip a tenant to `resident-anchored` via console.
Priya: Legal/Compliance: need retention of token issuance logs and ability to produce audit trail that a returned read had a resident-anchored proof for a timestamp/range.
legal-bot: (automated) Confirmed: retention policy required = 2 years for EU PII contracts.
Dan: Rough schedule: 2 sprints to prototype proof issuer + validator, 1 sprint for SDK & API opt-in, 1 sprint stabilization + canary.
Priya: I'll write a concise RFC follow-up capturing header semantics, token format, runbook, and test matrix. Any objections?
Carlos: None from infra.
Yvonne: None.
legal-bot: No objections, pending compliance sign-off after RFC.
ops-bot: :thumbsup:
